chunks: Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz narrated that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) was asked about a man who transfers a debt to another man, asking: Does it return to him?
He said: 'It does not return to him ever, unless he had gone bankrupt before that.'

key_terms.أَفْلَسَ: To go bankrupt or become insolvent.
key_terms.يَرْجِعُ: To return or revert (in this context, the debt reverting to the original creditor).
key_terms.يُحِيلُ: To transfer a debt or assign a claim to another party.

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on reclaiming a transferred debt in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi records this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) regarding the irrevocability of debt assignment (hiyal), establishing that the original creditor retains no claim against the debtor once the transfer is complete, unless the assignee becomes insolvent prior to settlement. This highlights the Shia jurisprudential emphasis on the finality of contractual transfers and the specific conditions under which the original creditor may seek recourse, reflecting the practical legal dynamics of trade in early Islamic society.
